full_name: Variance-Reduced Accelerated Gradient Descent for Smooth Convex and Strongly Convex Finite-Sum Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Theorem 5.9)

problem.description: Composite finite-sum optimization problem used by Section 5.4.

variable_space.math: X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^m\text{ is a closed convex set},\quad f(x)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x),\quad h\text{ is a simple but possibly nondifferentiable convex function}

assumptions.name: Component convexity
assumptions.math: X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^m\text{ is a closed convex set, }f\text{ is the average of }m\text{ smooth convex component functions }f_i,\text{ i.e., }f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)/m,\text{ and }h\text{ is a simple but possibly non-differentiable convex function}

assumptions.name: Possible strong convexity
assumptions.math: f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle \nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\mu V(x,y),\quad \forall x,y\in X

assumptions.name: Convexity of h
assumptions.math: h\text{ is a simple but possibly nondifferentiable convex function}

assumptions.name: Strongly convex epoch cutoff size facts

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Suppose that the probabilities }q_i\text{'s are set to }L_i/\sum_{i=1}^m L_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m.\ \text{Moreover, let us denote }s_0:=\lfloor\log m\rfloor+1\text{ and assume that the weights }\{\theta_t\}\text{ are set to (5.4.12) if }1\le s\le s_0\text{ or }s_0<s\le s_0+\sqrt{\frac{12L}{m\mu}}-4,\ m<\frac{3L}{4\mu}.\ \text{Otherwise, they are set to (5.4.26). If the parameters }\{T_s\},\{\gamma_s\},\text{ and }\{p_s\}\text{ set to (5.4.17) with }\{\alpha_s\}\text{ given by (5.4.25), then we have }\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x^*)]\le \begin{cases}2^{-(s+1)}D_0,&1\le s\le s_0,\\ \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^sD_0,&s>s_0\text{ and }m\ge \frac{3L}{4\mu},\\ \frac{16D_0}{(s-s_0+4)^2m},&s_0<s\le s_0+\sqrt{\frac{12L}{m\mu}}-4\text{ and }m<\frac{3L}{4\mu},\\ \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{3mL}}\right)^{-m(s-\bar{s}_0)/2}\frac{D_0}{3L/(4\mu)},&s_0+\sqrt{\frac{12L}{m\mu}}-4=\bar{s}_0<s\text{ and }m<\frac{3L}{4\mu},\end{cases}\ \text{where }x^*\text{ is an optimal solution of (5.3.1) and }D_0\text{ is defined as in (5.4.20).}
main_theorem.rate: Corollary 5.11 gives total component-gradient bounds O(m log(D0/eps)), O(m log m + sqrt(m D0/eps)), or O(m log m + sqrt(mL/mu) log((D0/eps)/(3L/(4mu)))) according to the three regimes.

proof.description: The theorem fixes the nonuniform probabilities, the switching rule for theta_t, the parameter policy (5.4.17) with alpha_s from (5.4.25), and the printed prerequisites that x* is an optimal solution of (5.3.1) and D0 is defined by (5.4.20).
For 1 <= s <= s0, invoke the first-phase bound.
For s > s0 and m >= 3L/(4mu), invoke the large-m linear contraction lemma.
For the intermediate small-m range, invoke Lemma 5.20.
For s > sbar0 in the small-m range, invoke Lemma 5.21 with sbar0 as printed in Theorem 5.9.
The four case bounds are exactly the piecewise statement (5.4.32), with x* optimal for (5.3.1) and D0 from (5.4.20).

key_lemmas.name: Accelerated variance estimator facts (Section 5.4)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Similar to the results (i.e., (5.3.6) and (5.3.7)) in Lemma 5.13, we have, conditionally on }x_1,\ldots,x_t,\quad \mathbb{E}[\delta_t]=0,\qquad \mathbb{E}[\|\delta_t\|_*^2]\le 2L_Q[f(\tilde{x})-f(\underline{x}_t)-\langle \nabla f(\underline{x}_t),\tilde{x}-\underline{x}_t\rangle]
key_lemmas.role: Provides the accelerated-search-point conditional unbiasedness and variance bound used inside Lemma 5.16.

proof.description: Define the accelerated residual and record the paper's explicit Section 5.4 transfer of Lemma 5.13's first two conclusions to Algorithm 5.7.

key_lemmas.name: Two-center Bregman prox inequality (Lemma 3.5)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let the convex function }p:X\to\mathbb{R},\text{ the points }\tilde{x},\tilde{y}\in X,\text{ and the scalars }\mu_1,\mu_2\ge 0\text{ be given. Let }\nu:X\to\mathbb{R}\text{ be a differentiable convex function and }V(x,z)\text{ be defined in (3.2.2). If }\hat{u}\in\operatorname*{Argmin}\{p(u)+\mu_1V(\tilde{x},u)+\mu_2V(\tilde{y},u):u\in X\},\text{ then for any }u\in X,\ p(\hat{u})+\mu_1V(\tilde{x},\hat{u})+\mu_2V(\tilde{y},\hat{u})\le p(u)+\mu_1V(\tilde{x},u)+\mu_2V(\tilde{y},u)-(\mu_1+\mu_2)V(\hat{u},u)
key_lemmas.role: Applied to the prox update defining x_t in Algorithm 5.7.

proof.description: From the definition of uhat and differentiable convexity of V(tilde{x}, .), introduce the paper's subgradient witness p'(uhat) in partial p(uhat) and record the resulting variational inequality.
proof.math: p'(\hat{u})\in\partial p(\hat{u}),\qquad \langle p'(\hat{u})+\mu_1\nabla V(\tilde{x},\hat{u})+\mu_2\nabla V(\tilde{y},\hat{u}),u-\hat{u}\rangle\ge 0,\quad \forall u\in X

proof.description: Use the three-point identity following from the definition of V.
Expand the two Bregman terms V(tilde{x},u) and V(tilde{y},u) by applying the three-point identity to each center.
Use convexity of p with the displayed subgradient witness p'(uhat) to replace p(u) by p(uhat)+<p'(uhat),u-uhat>, preserving the inner-product term printed by the paper.
Apply the variational inequality from the prox optimality condition to lower-bound the inner-product term by zero.
Rearrange the final lower bound by subtracting (mu_1+mu_2)V(uhat,u) from the right-hand side to obtain the statement of Lemma 3.5.

key_lemmas.name: One-step accelerated prox inequality (Lemma 5.15)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{For any }x\in X,\text{ we have }\gamma_s[l_f(\underline{x}_t,x_t)-l_f(\underline{x}_t,x)+h(x_t)-h(x)]\le \gamma_s\mu V(\underline{x}_t,x)+V(x_{t-1},x)-(1+\mu\gamma_s)V(x_t,x)-\frac{1+\mu\gamma_s}{2}\|x_t-x_{t-1}^+\|^2-\gamma_s\langle \delta_t,x_t-x\rangle
key_lemmas.role: Transforms the Algorithm 5.7 prox update into the basic one-step inequality used in Lemma 5.16.

proof.description: Apply Lemma 3.5 to the definition of x_t in Algorithm 5.7.
Rewrite the sampled-gradient inner product as the f-linearization gap plus the residual inner product.
Lower-bound the two Bregman prox terms by squared norms using the prox strong-convexity lower bound and the modulus-one normalization.
Lower-bound the squared-norm expression by the x_{t-1}^+ distance; the paper justifies this by the definition of x_{t-1}^+ in (5.4.3) and the convexity of \|\cdot\|^2.
Combine the prox update inequality, inner-product rewrite, and the two norm lower bounds.

key_lemmas.name: Conditional one-step recursion (Lemma 5.16)
key_lemmas.statement_math:
Assume that \alpha_s\in[0,1], p_s\in[0,1], and \gamma_s>0 satisfy
\[
1+\mu\gamma_s-L\alpha_s\gamma_s>0, \tag{5.4.7}
\]
\[
p_s-\frac{L_Q\alpha_s\gamma_s}{1+\mu\gamma_s-L\alpha_s\gamma_s}\ge 0. \tag{5.4.8}
\]
Then, conditional on x_1,\ldots,x_{t-1}, we have
\[
\frac{\gamma_s}{\alpha_s}\mathbb{E}[\psi(\bar{x}_t)-\psi(x)]+(1+\mu\gamma_s)\mathbb{E}[V(x_t,x)]\le \frac{\gamma_s}{\alpha_s}(1-\alpha_s-p_s)\mathbb{E}[\psi(\bar{x}_{t-1})-\psi(x)]+\frac{\gamma_s p_s}{\alpha_s}\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x})-\psi(x)]+\mathbb{E}[V(x_{t-1},x)] \tag{5.4.9}
\]
for any x\in X.
key_lemmas.role: The central inner-loop recursion summed in Lemmas 5.17-5.21.

proof.description: Record the local hypotheses of Lemma 5.16: alpha_s in [0,1], p_s in [0,1], gamma_s>0, together with (5.4.7) and (5.4.8). These are hypotheses of this lemma, not independent assumptions for Theorem 5.9.
Use smoothness of f and the definition of bar{x}_t, then substitute (5.4.6).
Insert Lemma 5.15 into the alpha_s l_f term and use strong convexity of f to replace linearizations by function values where printed.
Use strong convexity/convexity to bound the first linearized term by f(bar{x}_{t-1}) and split the residual inner product into x_t-x_{t-1}^+ plus x_{t-1}^+-x.
Apply Cauchy-Schwarz/Young to absorb the x_t-x_{t-1}^+ residual into the negative squared-distance term.

Condition on x_1,...,x_{t-1}; use the zero mean residual (5.4.4) to remove the last inner product and the variance bound (5.4.5) to replace the squared residual term by the printed gradient-gap expression.
Collect the l_f(underlined x_t, tilde{x}) coefficient and the f(tilde{x}) coefficient exactly as in the displayed chain.
Apply condition (5.4.8) and convexity of f, so the nonnegative l_f coefficient can be bounded by replacing l_f(underlined x_t, tilde{x}) with f(tilde{x}).
Add convexity of h along the same convex combination defining bar{x}_t.
Sum the previous conclusions to get (5.4.10)-(5.4.11).
Subtract Psi(x) from both sides and rearrange to the displayed conditional recursion (5.4.9).

key_lemmas.name: Smooth epoch recursion (Lemma 5.17)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Assume that for each epoch }s,\ s\ge 1,\ \alpha_s,\gamma_s,p_s,\text{ and }T_s\text{ are chosen such that (5.4.7)--(5.4.8) hold. Also, let }\theta_t=\begin{cases}\frac{\gamma_s}{\alpha_s}(\alpha_s+p_s),&t=1,\ldots,T_s-1,\\ \frac{\gamma_s}{\alpha_s},&t=T_s,\end{cases}\ L_s:=\frac{\gamma_s}{\alpha_s}+(T_s-1)\frac{\gamma_s(\alpha_s+p_s)}{\alpha_s},\ R_s:=\frac{\gamma_s}{\alpha_s}(1-\alpha_s)+(T_s-1)\frac{\gamma_sp_s}{\alpha_s},\ w_s:=L_s-R_{s+1}\ge 0,\ \forall s\ge 1.\ \text{Then }L_s\mathbb{E}[\Psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\Psi(x)]+\left(\sum_{j=1}^{s-1}w_j\right)\mathbb{E}[\Psi(\bar{x}^s)-\Psi(x)]\le R_1\mathbb{E}[\Psi(\tilde{x}^0)-\Psi(x)]+V(x^0,x)-V(x^s,x),\ \text{where }\bar{x}^s:=\left(\sum_{j=1}^{s-1}w_j\right)^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{s-1}w_j\tilde{x}^j.
key_lemmas.role: The smooth-case multi-epoch telescope reused in Lemma 5.20.

proof.description: Record the local hypothesis in Lemma 5.17 that the epoch parameters are chosen so that (5.4.7)--(5.4.8) hold; this is the assumption that permits using Lemma 5.16 after setting mu=0.
proof.ref: Lemma 5.17 statement and proof, lines 17083-17106; Eqs. (5.4.7)-(5.4.8)
proof.math: \text{Assume that for each epoch }s,\ s\ge 1,\ \alpha_s,\gamma_s,p_s,\text{ and }T_s\text{ are chosen such that (5.4.7)--(5.4.8) hold.}

proof.description: Set mu=0 in Lemma 5.16.
Sum over t=1,...,T_s, use theta_t from (5.4.12), xbar_0=tilde{x}, and rearrange.
Use x^s=x_T, tilde{x}^s as the weighted average, tilde{x}=tilde{x}^{s-1}, and convexity of Psi.
Identify the sum of weights with L_s and the coefficient with R_s.
Sum the single-epoch recursions, use convexity of Psi for the cross-epoch weighted average \bar{x}^s, and rearrange with w_s=L_s-R_{s+1}.

key_lemmas.name: Smooth-case proof facts (Theorem 5.8)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Assume that }\theta_t\text{ are defined in (5.4.12) and the probabilities }q_i\text{ are set to }L_i/\sum_{i=1}^m L_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m.\ \text{Moreover, let us denote }s_0:=\lfloor\log_2 m\rfloor+1\text{ and assume that }T_s=\begin{cases}2^{s-1},&s\le s_0,\\ T_{s_0},&s>s_0,\end{cases}\quad \gamma_s=\frac{1}{3L\alpha_s},\quad p_s=\frac{1}{2},\quad \alpha_s=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{2},&s\le s_0,\\ \frac{2}{s-s_0+4},&s>s_0.\end{cases}\ \text{Then for any }x\in X,\quad \mathbb{E}[\Psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\Psi(x)]\le \begin{cases}2^{-(s+1)}D_0,&1\le s\le s_0,\\ \frac{8LD_0}{(s-s_0+4)^2(m+1)},&s>s_0,\end{cases}\quad \text{where }D_0:=2[\psi(x^0)-\psi(x^*)]+3LV(x^0,x^*).
key_lemmas.role: Supplies the smooth-case coefficient checks, w_s nonnegativity, R_1 value, and L_s lower bound (5.4.21) reused in Lemma 5.20 and Lemma 5.21.

proof.description: With q_i=L_i/sum_i L_i, identify L_Q=L and verify the two Lemma 5.16 conditions under the smooth-case schedule printed in Theorem 5.8.
For 1 <= s < s0, compute w_s=L_s-R_{s+1} using alpha_{s+1}=alpha_s, gamma_{s+1}=gamma_s, and T_{s+1}=2T_s.
For s >= s0, compute w_s=L_s-R_{s+1} and show it is nonnegative.
Use the verified side conditions and w_s nonnegativity to instantiate Lemma 5.17 in its full displayed form, retaining the cross-epoch weighted-average term and the endpoint -V(x^s,x).
Record the theorem proof's printed iterative consequence for arbitrary x in X after applying the verified coefficient observations in (5.4.15), preserving the paper's arbitrary-x transition.
Apply Bregman nonnegativity to the printed arbitrary-x bound to discard the nonpositive endpoint -V(x^s,x), then use the printed fact R_1=2/(3L) together with tilde{x}^0=x^0.
Compute L_s in the two regimes: the proof first records the exact first-phase value for s <= s0, and then records the s >= s0 formula and lower bound (5.4.21).

Specialize the preceding arbitrary-x inequality to the optimal solution x^*. This is the needed bridge from the printed bound with free x to the D_0 endpoint, since D_0 in (5.4.20) is defined using x^*.

Combine the x=x^* specialization with the two L_s estimates. For s <= s0 use L_s=2^{s+1}/(3L); for s>s0 use L_s >= (s-s0+4)^2(m+1)/(24L). Together with D_0=2[\psi(x^0)-\psi(x^*)]+3LV(x^0,x^*) this gives the two printed D_0 rates with x^* on the comparison point.

Use optimality of x^* for (5.3.1) to compare the arbitrary theorem statement with the x^* bound: for any x in X, \Psi(x^*)<=\Psi(x), hence the arbitrary-x left side is bounded above by the already established x^* left side. This recovers the paper's displayed for-any-x conclusion (5.4.19).
proof.ref: Theorem 5.8 statement lines 17160-17170; Theorem 5.8 proof line 17221; Eq. (5.4.20)

key_lemmas.name: Smooth gradient complexity bound (Corollary 5.10)
key_lemmas.statement_math:
The total number of gradient evaluation performed by the variance-reduced accelerated gradient method can be bounded by
\[
\bar{N}:=\begin{cases}O\left(m\log\frac{D_0}{\varepsilon}\right),&m\varepsilon\ge D_0,\\ O\left(\sqrt{\frac{mD_0}{\varepsilon}}+m\log m\right),&\text{o.w.}\end{cases} \tag{5.4.22}
\]
where D_0 is defined in (5.4.20).
key_lemmas.role: Supplies the smooth-case component-gradient bounds (5.4.23) and (5.4.24) explicitly invoked at the start of Corollary 5.11.

proof.description: In the lower-accuracy and/or large-component regime m epsilon >= D0, the proof first observes the target is reached within s0 epochs and defines the bounded epoch count S_l.
Use the first-regime epoch count and T_s=2^{s-1} to obtain the printed smooth complexity bound (5.4.23).
In the high-accuracy and/or smaller-component regime m epsilon < D0, the proof records the total epoch bound S_h.
Split the gradient evaluations into the first s0 epochs and the remaining epochs, then simplify to the printed high-accuracy smooth bound (5.4.24).

key_lemmas.name: First-phase epoch decay (Lemma 5.18)
key_lemmas.statement_math:
If s\le s_0, then for any x\in X,
\[
\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x)]\le 2^{-(s+1)}D_0,\quad 1\le s\le s_0,
\]
where D_0 is defined in (5.4.20).
key_lemmas.role: Gives the first case of Theorem 5.9 and the base bound for later cases.

proof.description: Before applying Lemma 5.16, derive its side conditions from the first-phase schedule. The schedule gives alpha_s=p_s=1/2 and gamma_s=1/(3L alpha_s)=2/(3L), hence alpha_s,p_s in [0,1] and gamma_s>0. With q_i=L_i/sum_i L_i, L_Q=L; therefore 1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s=2/3+mu gamma_s>0 and p_s-L_Q alpha_s gamma_s/(1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s)>=1/2-(1/3)/(2/3)=0.
In the first phase set alpha_s=p_s=1/2, gamma_s=2/(3L), and T_s=2^{s-1}; substitute these into (5.4.9).
Sum over t=1,...,T_s, retaining the nonnegative mu gamma_s sum.
Use theta_t=gamma_s/alpha_s, the epoch identities tilde{x}=tilde{x}^{s-1}, x_0=x^{s-1}, x^s=x_{T_s}, and T_s=2T_{s-1}.
Apply the epoch recursion repeatedly back to s=0.
Apply Bregman nonnegativity to (5.4.27) while preserving the paper's arbitrary x in X boundary, so the left Bregman term can be dropped before the final T_s substitution.
Specialize the objective-only consequence of (5.4.27) to x=x^*. This keeps the paper's arbitrary-x derivation boundary but moves to the comparison point used in D_0.
Plug T_s=2^{s-1} into the x=x^* objective bound. With D_0=2[\psi(x^0)-\psi(x^*)]+3LV(x^0,x^*) from (5.4.20), this identifies the D_0 bound for the optimal comparison point.

Use optimality of x^* for (5.3.1) to pass from the x^* comparison to the lemma's printed for-any-x conclusion: for any x in X, \psi(x^*)<=\psi(x), so \mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x)]<=\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x^*)].

key_lemmas.name: First-phase Lyapunov relation (Eq. 5.4.27)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \frac{4T_s}{3L}\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x)]+\mathbb{E}[V(x^s,x)]\le \frac{2}{3L}\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^0)-\psi(x)]+V(x^0,x)=\frac{2}{3L}\mathbb{E}[\psi(x^0)-\psi(x)]+V(x^0,x)
key_lemmas.role: Exposes the printed Lyapunov relation used in Lemmas 5.19 and 5.20, separately from Lemma 5.18's final objective-only decay.

proof.description: Before applying Lemma 5.16, derive its side conditions from the first-phase schedule. The schedule gives alpha_s=p_s=1/2 and gamma_s=1/(3L alpha_s)=2/(3L), hence alpha_s,p_s in [0,1] and gamma_s>0. With q_i=L_i/sum_i L_i, L_Q=L; therefore 1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s=2/3+mu gamma_s>0 and p_s-L_Q alpha_s gamma_s/(1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s)>=1/2-(1/3)/(2/3)=0.
In the first phase substitute alpha_s=p_s=1/2, gamma_s=2/(3L), and T_s=2^{s-1} into (5.4.9).

Apply the epoch recursion repeatedly back to s=0 to obtain the printed Lyapunov relation.

key_lemmas.name: Smooth L_s lower bounds (Eq. 5.4.21)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{if }s\le s_0,\ L_s=\frac{2^{s+1}}{3L}.\quad \text{if }s\ge s_0,\ L_s=\frac{1}{3L\alpha_s^2}\left[1+(T_s-1)\left(\alpha_s+\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]=\frac{(s-s_0+4)(T_{s_0}-1)}{6L}+\frac{(s-s_0+4)^2(T_{s_0}+1)}{24L}\ge \frac{(s-s_0+4)^2(m+1)}{24L}
key_lemmas.role: Exposes the printed coefficient lower bound (5.4.21) and its T_{s0}-based specializations used in Lemmas 5.20 and 5.21.

proof.description: The smooth-case proof computes L_s directly from the coefficient definition in the first phase and for s >= s0.
Using T_{s0}=2^{\lfloor\log_2 m\rfloor} >= m/2, record the specialized lower bound used in Lemma 5.20.

key_lemmas.name: Linear contraction for large m (Lemma 5.19)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{If }s\ge s_0\text{ and }m\ge \frac{3L}{4\mu},\quad \mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x^*)]\le \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^sD_0,\quad \text{where }x^*\text{ is an optimal solution of (5.3.1).}
key_lemmas.role: Gives Theorem 5.9's large-m strongly convex branch.

proof.description: Before applying Lemma 5.16, derive its side conditions in the large-m strongly convex regime. The printed schedule gives alpha_s=p_s=1/2, gamma_s=2/(3L), and T_s=T_{s0}; hence alpha_s,p_s in [0,1] and gamma_s>0. Since q_i=L_i/sum_i L_i implies L_Q=L and mu>=0, (5.4.7) is 1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s=2/3+mu gamma_s>0, and (5.4.8) follows from p_s-L_Q alpha_s gamma_s/(1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s)>=1/2-(1/3)/(2/3)=0.
In this case alpha_s=p_s=1/2, gamma_s=2/(3L), and T_s=T_{s0}; substitute into (5.4.9).
Multiply by Gamma_{t-1}=(1+2mu/(3L))^{t-1}.
Since theta_t=Gamma_{t-1}, sum over the inner loop and telescope the V terms.
Use m >= T_s0 >= m/2 and m >= 3L/(4mu) to lower-bound Gamma_{T_s}.
uses: Strongly convex epoch cutoff size facts

proof.description: Use the weighted-average definition of tilde{x}^s, epoch identities, (5.4.28), and the fact \psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x^*)\ge 0 from x^* being an optimal solution.

Plug (5.4.27) into the preceding inequality and simplify to the printed bound.

key_lemmas.name: Case 3 strong-convex epoch recursion (Lemma 5.20 proof)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{In this case, }\frac{1}{2}\ge \frac{2}{s-s_0+4}\ge \sqrt{\frac{m\mu}{3L}}.\ \text{Therefore, we set }\theta_t\text{ as in (5.4.12), }\alpha_s=\frac{2}{s-s_0+4},\ p_s=\frac{1}{2},\ \gamma_s=\frac{1}{3L\alpha_s},\ \text{and }T_s\equiv T_{s_0}.
key_lemmas.role: Records the strong-convex analogue of the smooth epoch procedure used to obtain the first inequality of (5.4.29) without invoking the mu=0 Lemma 5.17 directly.

proof.description: Identify Case 3 from the printed range and parameter choices: theta_t is (5.4.12), alpha_s=2/(s-s0+4), p_s=1/2, gamma_s=1/(3L alpha_s), and T_s=T_s0.

Verify the Lemma 5.16 side conditions from the Case 3 printed schedule. From 1/2 >= 2/(s-s0+4) >= sqrt(m mu/(3L)), alpha_s=2/(s-s0+4) lies in [0,1], p_s=1/2 lies in [0,1], and gamma_s=1/(3L alpha_s)>0. With q_i=L_i/sum_i L_i, L_Q=L; hence 1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s=2/3+mu gamma_s>0 and p_s-L_Q alpha_s gamma_s/(1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s)>=1/2-(1/3)/(2/3)=0.
Apply Lemma 5.16 under the Case 3 schedule while retaining the printed strong-convex distance multiplier (1+mu gamma_s), rather than setting mu=0.

Sum the retained strong-convex recursion over t=1,...,T_s with theta_t from (5.4.12), xbar_0=tilde{x}, and the epoch identities. This gives the smooth single-epoch left side plus the additional nonnegative derived residual mu gamma_s sum_t E[V(x_t,x)].
proof.ref: Lemma 5.17 proof lines 17107-17133 by the procedure cited at Lemma 5.20 lines 17474-17475

proof.description: Drop the additional nonnegative strong-convex residual from the left side, yielding the same single-epoch L_j/R_j inequality used in the smooth procedure but with the distance term still present.

key_lemmas.name: Intermediate Lyapunov bound (Eq. 5.4.29)
key_lemmas.statement_math: L_s\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x)]+\mathbb{E}[V(x^s,x)]\le R_{s_0+1}\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^{s_0})-\psi(x)]+\mathbb{E}[V(x^{s_0},x)]\le L_{s_0}\mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^{s_0})-\psi(x)]+\mathbb{E}[V(x^{s_0},x)]\le \frac{D_0}{3L}
key_lemmas.role: Exposes the Case 3 Lyapunov display used both to prove Lemma 5.20 and to initialize the tail proof in Lemma 5.21.

proof.description: In Case 3 the parameter setting is the same as the smooth case in Theorem 5.8, so the proof follows the same L_s, R_s, w_s procedure.

Apply the Case 3 strong-convex epoch recursion, obtained by following the Theorem 5.8 coefficient procedure after retaining and dropping the nonnegative strong-convex residual, to compare epoch s against epoch s0.
Use the smooth-case coefficient comparison R_{s0+1} <= L_{s0}.

proof.ref: Eq. (5.4.29), third inequality and following sentence; Eq. (5.4.27); Eq. (5.4.20)

key_lemmas.name: Intermediate sublinear regime (Lemma 5.20)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{If }s_0<s\le s_0+\sqrt{\frac{12L}{m\mu}}-4\text{ and }m<\frac{3L}{4\mu},\text{ then for any }x\in X,\quad \mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x)]\le \frac{16D_0}{(s-s_0+4)^2m}.
key_lemmas.role: Gives the small-m pre-tail branch of Theorem 5.9 and initializes Lemma 5.21.

proof.description: In this range, identify the schedule with the smooth-case schedule: alpha_s=2/(s-s0+4), p_s=1/2, gamma_s=1/(3L alpha_s), and T_s=T_s0.
Invoke the separately recorded Case 3 Lyapunov chain (5.4.29), preserving the PDF's printed arbitrary-x display before the D_0 specialization bridge.
Use the x=x^* specialization exposed in the proof of (5.4.29) to get L_s E[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x^*)] <= D_0/(3L), after dropping the nonnegative Bregman term.

Use optimality of x^* for (5.3.1) to recover Lemma 5.20's arbitrary-x objective-only conclusion: for any x in X, \psi(x^*)<=\psi(x), hence E[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x)]<=E[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x^*)].
proof.ref: Lemma 5.20 statement and proof, lines 17467-17483; Eq. (5.4.20)

key_lemmas.name: Accelerated linear tail (Lemma 5.21)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{If }s>\bar{s}_0:=s_0+\sqrt{\frac{12L}{m\mu}}-4\text{ and }m<\frac{3L}{4\mu},\quad \mathbb{E}[\psi(\tilde{x}^s)-\psi(x^*)]\le \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{3mL}}\right)^{-m(s-\bar{s}_0)/2}\frac{D_0}{3L/(4\mu)},\quad \text{where }x^*\text{ is an optimal solution of (5.3.1).}
key_lemmas.role: Gives Theorem 5.9's final small-m accelerated linear branch.

proof.description: In the tail regime choose the constant policy alpha_s=sqrt(m mu/(3L)), p_s=1/2, gamma_s=1/sqrt(3mLmu), T_s=T_s0, and theta_t by (5.4.26).

Verify the Lemma 5.16 side conditions from the constant tail schedule. The tail regime m<3L/(4mu) gives 0<alpha_s=sqrt(m mu/(3L))<1/2, while p_s=1/2 and gamma_s=1/(3L alpha_s)>0. With q_i=L_i/sum_i L_i, L_Q=L; thus 1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s=2/3+mu gamma_s>0 and p_s-L_Q alpha_s gamma_s/(1+mu gamma_s-L alpha_s gamma_s)>=1/2-(1/3)/(2/3)=0.
Multiply (5.4.9) by Gamma_{t-1}=(1+mu gamma_s)^{t-1}.
Sum from t=1 to T_s and use xbar_0=tilde{x}.
Use epoch identities, the definition of tilde{x}^s, and convexity of psi to obtain (5.4.31).
Expand the sum of theta_t using (5.4.26).
Record the printed auxiliary inequalities for the tail coefficient: the elementary power bound and the alpha_s lower bound implied by the constant policy.

proof.description: Instantiate the printed power-bound side condition with delta=mu gamma_s and T=T_{s0}-1: from T_{s0}<=m and gamma_s=1/sqrt(3mLmu), mu gamma_s(T_{s0}-1)<=mu gamma_s m=sqrt(m mu/(3L)); the tail regime m<3L/(4mu) makes this <1/2, so 0<=mu gamma_s(T_{s0}-1)<=1.

Lower-bound the bracket coefficient by gamma_s p_s T_s0/alpha_s using the printed observation after the constant tail policy is restated.

key_lemmas.name: Gradient complexity bound (Corollary 5.11)
key_lemmas.statement_math:
The total number of gradient evaluations of f_i performed by Algorithm 5.7 to find a stochastic \varepsilon-solution of (2.0.1) can be bounded by
\[
\bar{N}:=\begin{cases}O\left(m\log\frac{D_0}{\varepsilon}\right),&m\ge \frac{D_0}{\varepsilon}\text{ or }m\ge \frac{3L}{4\mu},\\ O\left(m\log m+\sqrt{\frac{mD_0}{\varepsilon}}\right),&m<\frac{D_0}{\varepsilon}\le \frac{3L}{4\mu},\\ O\left(m\log m+\sqrt{\frac{mL}{\mu}}\log\frac{D_0/\varepsilon}{3L/(4\mu)}\right),&m<\frac{3L}{4\mu}\le \frac{D_0}{\varepsilon}.\end{cases} \tag{5.4.33}
\]
where D_0 is defined as in (5.4.20).
key_lemmas.role: Converts Theorem 5.9's rates into component-gradient complexity.

proof.description: The first and third cases of the convergence result (5.4.32) correspond to the smooth case discussed in Corollary 5.10, so the total gradient evaluations are bounded by (5.4.23) and (5.4.24), respectively.
For the second case of (5.4.32), the number of epochs is logarithmic and the total gradient count is bounded by (5.4.34).
For the last case of (5.4.32), record the printed upper bound on the number of epochs needed by the variance-reduced accelerated gradient method.
Split the total gradient count into the first phase, the intermediate phase, and the linear-tail phase.
Apply the printed bounds for s0, T_s0, sbar0-s0, and S-sbar0 to obtain the explicit numerical upper bound before big-O simplification.
